Cellular respiration converts chemical energy from glucose into ATP.

Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and produces pyruvate, ATP, and NADH.
The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
The electron transport chain uses a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane to produce most ATP.

Important comparison:
- Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and produces much more ATP.
- Fermentation regenerates NAD+ when oxygen is unavailable.
